what_it_does: Large language models are extremely sensitive to rounding: when you shrink numbers from 16-bit floats down to 4-bit integers (a process called quantization, which uses smaller, coarser numbers to save memory and speed up math), a mismatch in precision between different operations can hurt the model's accuracy or waste compute. Existing chips are locked into one such precision mode, so switching between, say, 4-bit weights multiplied by 16-bit activations versus fully 4-bit arithmetic requires different hardware or causes inefficiency. Precon is a chip architecture that can switch precision modes on the fly by sharing the same underlying arithmetic circuitry. Rather than building separate units for each combination, it routes data through a reconfigurable datapath that handles 4-bit times 16-bit, 4-bit times 4-bit, and 4-bit times 8-bit multiplications without rewiring the chip. This makes it practical to run diverse quantized models on a single piece of hardware without redesigning the silicon.
